projectCategory: DSA Module 2.2: Binary Heaps & Priority Queue Architectures
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: Max-Heap Array Implementation & Up-Heap (Bubble-Up) Insertion
projects.description: A Binary Heap is a complete binary tree stored compactly inside a 1D array where parent-child index relations are governed by simple formulas: `Left(i) = 2i + 1`, `Right(i) = 2i + 2`, and `Parent(i) = (i - 1) / 2`. In a Max-Heap, every parent node is greater than or equal to its children. In this project, you will construct a Max-Heap in C. `insert_max_heap()` appends new values at index `size` and bubbles up (`while (parent < child)` swapping elements) to restore heap order in O(log N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Complete Binary Trees, Implicit 1D Array Indexing & Up-Heap Bubble Swapping
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Max-Heap Up-Heap Insertion ---
Max-Heap: [ 40 30 20 10 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Append**: Place new key at end index `i = size++`.
2. **Bubble Up**: Compare with parent `(i - 1) / 2`. If `arr[parent] < arr[i]`, swap and move up.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `insert_max_heap()`: Performs up-heap bubble swapping to maintain Max-Heap invariant.

projects.title: Extract-Max from Max-Heap & Down-Heap (Heapify) Restoration
projects.description: Extracting the root (maximum element) from a Max-Heap requires replacing the root with the last leaf element, shrinking the size, and sifting down (`heapify_down`) by swapping with the larger child until heap order is restored. In this project, you will build an Extract-Max Engine in C in O(log N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Root Extraction, Down-Heap Sifting & O(log N) Priority Queue Deletion
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Extract-Max from Max-Heap ---
Extracted Root = 40
New Root = 30
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Root Replace**: Save `root = arr[0]`, overwrite `arr[0] = arr[size - 1]`, decrement `size--`.
2. **Down-Heap**: Compare root with left/right children. Swap with larger child recursively.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `extract_max()` & `heapify_down()`: Removes maximum element and restores heap invariant.

projects.title: Min-Heap Array Implementation & Up/Down-Heap Mechanics
projects.description: In a Min-Heap, every parent node is smaller than or equal to its children (`arr[parent] <= arr[child]`), making the root element the global minimum. In this project, you will construct a Min-Heap in C supporting dynamic insertion and root extraction in O(log N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Min-Heap Invariants, Root Minimum Access & Up/Down Sifting Dynamics
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Min-Heap Implementation ---
Min-Heap Root = 10
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Up-Heap**: Bubble up while `parent > child`.
2. **Min Root**: `arr[0]` is always global minimum.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `insert_min_heap()`: Implements Min-Heap array structure.

projects.title: Heapify Array in Linear O(N) Time (Floyd's Heap Construction)
projects.description: Building a heap by inserting N elements one-by-one takes O(N log N) time. Floyd's Heapify Algorithm converts an unsorted array into a valid heap in linear O(N) time! In this project, you will implement Floyd's Heap Construction in C by running `heapify_down()` on all non-leaf nodes starting from `(N/2 - 1)` down to 0.
projects.learningOutcome: Floyd's O(N) Heapify Algorithm, Bottom-Up Heap Building & Asymptotic Optimizations
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Floyd's O(N) Heapify Algorithm ---
Before: [ 4 10 3 5 1 ]
After : [ 10 5 3 4 1 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Non-Leaf Index**: Start at index `N/2 - 1`.
2. **Bottom-Up Loop**: Run `heapify_down(i)` decrementing `i` to 0.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `build_heap()`: Converts unsorted array to heap in linear O(N) time.

projects.title: Max-Heap Priority Queue Engine (Process Scheduler)
projects.description: Operating system process schedulers organize tasks by priority using a Priority Queue. Tasks with higher priority scores are dequeued first. In this project, you will build a Max-Heap Priority Queue Process Scheduler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Priority-Based Task Scheduling, Priority Queue Encapsulation & Operating System Integration
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Priority Queue Process Scheduler ---
Highest Priority Process PID = 102 (Priority = 9)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Struct Node**: Store `pid` and `priority`.
2. **Compare Priority**: Sift up/down based on process `priority` value.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `insert_pq()`: Priority queue scheduling engine.

projects.title: In-Place HeapSort Algorithm (Ascending Order)
projects.description: HeapSort is a comparison-based sorting algorithm that runs in O(N log N) worst-case time and O(1) auxiliary space! In this project, you will build HeapSort in C: (1) build Max-Heap in O(N) time, (2) swap root with last array element, and (3) shrink heap size and run `heapify()` on root.
projects.learningOutcome: In-Place HeapSort, O(N log N) Worst-Case Guarantee & Zero Extra Space Sorting
projects.exampleOutput:
--- In-Place HeapSort Algorithm ---
Before: [ 12 11 13 5 6 7 ]
Sorted: [ 5 6 7 11 12 13 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Build Heap**: `build_heap(arr, n)`.
2. **Sort Loop**: Swap `arr[0]` with `arr[i]`, run `heapify(arr, i, 0)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `heap_sort()`: Performs in-place HeapSort.

projects.title: Find K-th Largest Element in an Array using Min-Heap
projects.description: Finding the K-th largest number in an array can be solved using a Min-Heap of size K. Maintain the K largest elements in the Min-Heap; after processing all N elements, the root of the Min-Heap IS the K-th largest element! In this project, you will build K-th Largest Finder in C in O(N log K) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Bounded Size K Min-Heap, Stream Processing & O(N log K) Selection Strategy
projects.exampleOutput:
--- K-th Largest Element using Min-Heap ---
The 2-nd Largest Element = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Heap of Size K**: Store first K elements in Min-Heap.
2. **Stream Update**: If `arr[i] > root`, replace root and heapify.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `find_kth_largest()`: Solves K-th largest selection using size-K min-heap.

projects.title: Find K-th Smallest Element in an Array using Max-Heap
projects.description: To find the K-th smallest element, maintain a Max-Heap of size K. Process array elements: if `arr[i] < root`, replace root and heapify down. The Max-Heap root holds the K-th smallest element. In this project, you will implement K-th Smallest Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bounded Size K Max-Heap, Inverse Selection Mechanics & Stream Processing
projects.exampleOutput:
--- K-th Smallest Element using Max-Heap ---
The 3-rd Smallest Element = 7
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Heap of Size K**: Store first K elements in Max-Heap.
2. **Stream Update**: If `arr[i] < root`, replace root and heapify.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `find_kth_smallest()`: Solves K-th smallest selection using size-K max-heap.

projects.title: Check if an Array Represents a Valid Max-Heap
projects.description: Verify whether an array satisfies the Max-Heap structural property: for every internal index `i`, `arr[i] >= arr[2i + 1]` and `arr[i] >= arr[2i + 2]`. In this project, you will build a Max-Heap Validator in C operating in linear O(N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Heap Structural Inspection, Invariant Checking & Early Exit Bounds Verification
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Max-Heap Structural Validation ---
Array 1: Valid Max-Heap
Array 2: Invalid Heap
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Parent Loop**: Loop `i` from 0 to `(N - 2) / 2`.
2. **Child Verification**: Check `arr[i] >= arr[left]` and `arr[i] >= arr[right]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `is_max_heap()`: Validates heap structural property in O(N) time.

projects.title: Decrease-Key & Increase-Key Operations in Min/Max Heap
projects.description: Updating an element's value inside a heap requires re-sifting: `decrease_key` in a Min-Heap reduces a value and bubbles it up (`while parent > child`), while `increase_key` increases a value and sifts it down. In this project, you will implement Decrease-Key in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dynamic Priority Mutability, Key Alterations & Re-Sifting Operations
projects.exampleText: Decrease index 3 key to 5 in Min-Heap
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Min-Heap Decrease Key Operation ---
Before: [ 10 20 30 40 50 ]
After decreasing index 3 to 5: Root = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Overwrite**: Set `h[i] = new_val`.
2. **Bubble Up**: If `new_val < parent`, bubble up to restore Min-Heap invariant.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `decrease_key()`: Updates heap element value and bubbles up.

projects.title: Top K Frequent Elements Finder (Min-Heap Frequency Tracker)
projects.description: Given an array, find the K most frequent elements. Count element frequencies using a frequency table, then maintain a Min-Heap of size K ordered by frequency. In this project, you will build a Top K Frequent Elements Finder in C in O(N log K) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Frequency Table Hashing, Priority Queue Frequency Ranking & Top-K Extraction
projects.exampleText: Top K=2 frequent elements in dataset
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Top K Frequent Elements (K=2) ---
Element 4 (Freq 4)
Element 1 (Freq 3)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Tally Frequencies**: Build frequency table `(val, freq)`.
2. **Min-Heap**: Maintain Min-Heap of size K by `freq`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `heapify_min_freq()`: Maintains K most frequent items in Min-Heap.

projects.title: K-Way Merging of Sorted Arrays using Min-Heap
projects.description: Merge K sorted arrays into a single sorted array of size N*K. Instead of full array sorting in O(NK log NK), use a Min-Heap of size K containing the first unmerged element from each array. In this project, you will build a K-Way Merging Engine in C in O(NK log K) time.
projects.learningOutcome: K-Way Merging Algorithms, Multi-Stream Sorted Merging & O(NK log K) Complexity
projects.exampleOutput:
--- K-Way Merging of Sorted Arrays ---
Merged Array: [ 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Min-Heap Size K**: Insert `(arr[i][0], i, 0)` into Min-Heap.
2. **Extract & Advance**: Extract min, append to result, insert next element from same array into heap.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_heapify()`: Performs K-way sorted array merging using Min-Heap.

projects.title: Reorganize String (No Two Adjacent Same Characters) using Priority Queue
projects.description: Rearrange characters of a string so that no two adjacent characters are identical. Count character frequencies and greedily pick the two most frequent remaining characters using a Max-Heap. In this project, you will build a String Reorganization Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Greedy Scheduling, Frequency Priority Queue & Character Interleaving
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Reorganize String (No Adjacent Same Chars) ---
Before: aab
Reorganized String: aba
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Frequency Guard**: If `max_freq > (len + 1) / 2`, reorganization impossible.
2. **Greedy Placement**: Interleave most frequent character at even indices, then fill odd indices.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `reorganize_string()`: Reorganizes string characters to prevent adjacent duplicates.

projects.title: Connect N Ropes with Minimum Total Cost (Huffman-Style Min-Heap)
projects.description: Given N ropes of different lengths, connect them into one rope. The cost to connect two ropes is the sum of their lengths. Find the minimum total cost. Always connect the TWO SHORTEST ropes using a Min-Heap (Huffman Coding principle). In this project, you will build a Rope Connection Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Huffman Coding Strategy, Greedy Minimum Combination & Min-Heap Cost Minimization
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Connect Ropes with Minimum Total Cost ---
Minimum Total Connection Cost = 29
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Min-Heap**: Build Min-Heap of rope lengths.
2. **Extract Two Shortest**: Extract `r1` and `r2`, `cost = r1 + r2`, `total += cost`, insert `cost` back into heap.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `connect_ropes()`: Minimizes total connection cost using Min-Heap.

projects.title: Task Scheduler (CPU Cooling Periods) using Priority Queue
projects.description: Given a CPU task list and cooling period N between identical tasks, calculate minimum total CPU intervals required. Use a Max-Heap to schedule the highest frequency tasks first. In this project, you will build a CPU Task Scheduler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: CPU Task Scheduling, Cooling Period Management & Greedy Frequency Priority Queues
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Task Scheduler (CPU Cooling Periods) ---
Minimum Total Intervals Required = 8
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Count Frequencies**: Find max frequency `max_freq`.
2. **Cooling Slots**: `intervals = (max_freq - 1) * (N + 1) + max_freq_count`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `least_interval()`: Computes minimum CPU task scheduling intervals.

projects.title: K Closest Points to Origin (Euclidean Distance Heap Search)
projects.description: Given 2D points on a plane, find K closest points to origin `(0, 0)` using Euclidean distance squared `x^2 + y^2`. Maintain a Max-Heap of size K by distance squared. In this project, you will build a K Closest Points Finder in C in O(N log K) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Geometric Distance Heap Search, Size-K Max-Heap Bounding & O(N log K) Performance
projects.exampleOutput:
--- K Closest Points to Origin (K=2) ---
Point (-2, 2)
Point (1, 3)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Distance Squared**: `dist_sq = x^2 + y^2`.
2. **Size K Max-Heap**: Keep K smallest distance points in Max-Heap.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `max_heapify()`: Computes K closest points using Max-Heap.

projects.title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
projects.description: Given K sorted lists, find the smallest numerical range `[a, b]` that includes at least one number from each of the K lists. Maintain a Min-Heap of size K storing `(val, list_idx, elem_idx)`. In this project, you will build a Smallest Range Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Multi-List Range Bounding, Min-Heap Min/Max Tracking & Sliding Range Minimization
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Smallest Range Covering K Lists ---
Smallest Range bounds = [20, 24]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Min-Heap**: Store current element from each of K lists.
2. **Range Update**: `current_range = max_in_heap - min_in_heap`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `main()`: Finds smallest range containing elements from K sorted lists.

projects.title: Priority Queue with Arbitrary Key Deletion (Indexed Heap)
projects.description: Standard heaps do not support deleting an arbitrary item by index in O(log N) time because locating the item takes O(N) search time. An Indexed Priority Queue maintains an auxiliary inverse mapping array `qp[index]` pointing to the item's position in `pq[]`. In this project, you will build an Indexed Priority Queue in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Indexed Priority Queues, Inverse Position Arrays (`qp[]`) & Arbitrary O(log N) Deletions
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Indexed Priority Queue (Arbitrary Key Deletion) ---
Inserted 3 items into Indexed Min-PQ successfully.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dual Arrays**: `pq[heap_pos] = item_id` and `qp[item_id] = heap_pos`.
2. **O(log N) Key Update**: Access `qp[item_id]` in O(1) time and sift up/down in O(log N).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `init_ipq()` & `insert_ipq()`: Implements indexed priority queue with fast reverse lookups.

projects.title: Dynamic Median Maintenance from Continuous Data Stream (Dual Heap: Max + Min)
projects.description: Find the median of a stream of numbers in real-time. Use TWO heaps: a `Max-Heap` storing the smaller half of numbers and a `Min-Heap` storing the larger half of numbers. Balance heap sizes so `|MaxHeap.size - MinHeap.size| <= 1`. In this project, you will build a Dynamic Median Stream Engine in C in O(log N) per insertion.
projects.learningOutcome: Dual Heap Balancing Strategy, Real-Time Stream Median Tracking & O(1) Median Queries
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Continuous Stream Dynamic Median Maintenance ---
Stream input: [5, 15, 1, 3]
Dynamic Median after 4 elements = 4.0
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dual Heaps**: `MaxHeap` (left half), `MinHeap` (right half).
2. **Balance**: Keep size difference <= 1.
3. **Median Query**: If equal sizes, median is `(MaxHeap.root + MinHeap.root)/2.0`; else root of larger heap.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `max_heapify()` & `min_heapify()`: Maintains dynamic median using dual heap strategy.

projects.title: Maximum Sum Combination of Two Arrays using Priority Queue
projects.description: Given two arrays A and B of size N, find K maximum sum combinations `A[i] + B[j]`. Sort A and B in descending order, insert `A[0] + B[0]` into a Max-Heap, and extract K sums using a visited set. In this project, you will build a Max Sum Combination Engine in C in O(K log K) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Array Combination Ranking, Priority Queue Pair State & O(K log K) Combination Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Sum Combination of Two Arrays (K=3) ---
Top 3 Max Sum Combinations: [ 10 9 9 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sort Arrays**: Sort A and B in descending order.
2. **Max-Heap Pair Insert**: Insert `(A[0] + B[0], 0, 0)` into Max-Heap.
3. **Extract K Times**: Extract max sum, push next indices `(i+1, j)` and `(i, j+1)` into heap.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `max_heapify()`: Computes K maximum sum combinations of two arrays.

projects.title: Binomial Heap Implementation (Consolidate & Union Operations)
projects.description: A Binomial Heap is a collection of Binomial Trees satisfying binomial heap properties: key of node >= key of parent, and at most one binomial tree of any given degree. Merging two binomial heaps takes O(log N) time! In this project, you will build a Binomial Heap Skeleton in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Binomial Tree Forest, Degree Consolidation & Fast O(log N) Heap Union
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Binomial Heap Union & Consolidation Engine ---
Created Binomial Heap roots (10, 20) successfully.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Binomial Tree B_k**: Degree k tree formed by linking two B_{k-1} trees.
2. **Union Operation**: Merge root lists by degree and consolidate trees of equal degree.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `create_bnode()`: Binomial Heap node allocation and union skeleton.

projects.title: Fibonacci Heap Skeleton (Amortized O(1) Insert & Decrease-Key)
projects.description: A Fibonacci Heap is a loose collection of trees providing theoretical amortized constant time O(1) for `insert()`, `find_min()`, and `decrease_key()`, making it the engine behind Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm. In this project, you will build a Fibonacci Heap Skeleton in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Fibonacci Heap Data Structures, Amortized O(1) Operations & Circular Doubly Linked Roots
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Fibonacci Heap Amortized O(1) Engine ---
Fibonacci Heap Structure initialized for fast priority updates.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Circular Root List**: Roots stored in a circular doubly linked list.
2. **Cascading Cut**: Decrease-key cuts child and moves to root list, performing cascading cuts up parent path.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `main()`: Demonstrates Fibonacci Heap structure.

projects.title: D-Ary Heap Implementation (Branching Factor D Optimization for GPU/Cache)
projects.description: A D-Ary Heap is a generalization of binary heap where each node has D children instead of 2. For GPU architectures and CPU cache lines, D=4 or D=8 speeds up `decrease_key` and decreases heap height to `log_D(N)`. In this project, you will build a D-Ary Heap in C.
projects.learningOutcome: D-Ary Tree Branching, GPU/Cache Line Tuning & Index Formulas `D*i + 1` to `D*i + D`
projects.exampleOutput:
--- D-Ary Heap (Branching Factor D=4) ---
D-Ary Heap Root = 90
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Index Formulas**: `Children(i) = D*i + 1 .. D*i + D`, `Parent(i) = (i - 1) / D`.
2. **Shorter Height**: Height reduced by factor of `log_2(D)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `insert_dary()`: Implements D-Ary heap insertion.

projects.title: Minimum Candidate Cost for IPO / Maximum Capital Scheduler
projects.description: Given initial capital W and N projects with `capital[i]` requirements and `profits[i]`, select at most K distinct projects to maximize total final capital. Use a Min-Heap (ordered by capital required) and a Max-Heap (ordered by profit). In this project, you will build an IPO Project Scheduler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dual Heap Financial Scheduling, Available Capital Bounding & Maximizing Return on Investment
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Capital IPO Project Scheduler ---
Initial Capital: 0
Final Maximized Capital = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Min-Heap Capital**: Move all affordable projects `capital[i] <= W` into Max-Heap profits.
2. **Max-Heap Profit**: Extract max profit project, add profit to `W`, repeat K times.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `find_max_capital()`: Greedy project scheduling using priority queues.

projects.title: Cache-Oblivious Implicit Heap Layout for High-Throughput Memory Subsystems
projects.description: Standard binary heap array traversal suffers cache line misses at deep levels because children `2i + 1` jump across RAM pages. A Cache-Oblivious Heap aligns subtrees into B-Tree sized memory blocks (e.g. 64-byte blocks), achieving optimal CPU L1/L2 cache locality. In this project, you will build a Cache-Oblivious Heap Layout Inspector in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Cache-Oblivious Data Structures, L1/L2 CPU Cache Alignment & Memory Subsystem Throughput
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Cache-Oblivious Implicit Heap Layout ---
B-Tree sub-block aligned heap array eliminates L1 cache line misses.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sub-block Alignment**: Recursive van Emde Boas or block-aligned array mapping.
2. **Zero Cache Misses**: Guarantees optimal cache transfers regardless of cache block size.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cache_oblivious_layout_demo()`: Cache-oblivious heap memory layout demonstration.
